correctness.rationale: The exact frontier is correct, but the frozen opening is misleading if read as saying the angle provides information beyond the norm at fixed step size. In this family (I−R)^T(I−R)=2(1−cos θ)I, so the norm and the cosine identify one another. The complete repaired RESULT gives the equivalent norm thresholds and clarifies their dependence on the step size. Independently reconstructing the complex two-by-two update gives P=2u−2u²t²z and Q=u²(1−t²z). The determinant modulus is strictly below one. For roots a,b, the Schur difference equals (1−|a|²)(1−|b|²)|1−a conjugate(b)|²; hence its positive, zero or negative sign decides both strict stability and the exact radius-one boundary. Expanding yields the prefactor (1+c) times the sign factor c−H(t), with c=cos θ. At c=−1 the two roots are 1 and (1+t²)/(1+t)², including for t above the matched cutoff. Factoring H±1 and differentiating proves the two transitions and strict monotonicity; substitution gives H(2)=−11/25. value.rationale: For a standard splitting algorithm, the exact model tests what generic sufficient mismatch estimates miss. The frontier identifies a sharp safe region, distinguishes a fixed-point obstruction from an expanding mode, and yields explicit changes in angular tolerance, including convergence at a substantial mismatch beyond familiar matched sufficient step restrictions. The purpose survives the clarification that in this rotation family the norm is already a complete angular parameter at each fixed t.
